flame:
Create a production sprite sheet of an industrial machinery FIRE effect for the game BrineSpace. The two supplied images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: their fixed elevated south-facing cutaway camera, deliberately drawn pixel clusters, rich restrained detail, muted engineering materials, and realistic rather than cartoon game-art language. Do not reproduce any room, machinery, metal platform, floor, border, letters, or background.

OUTPUT: exactly one 1536x1024 RGBA PNG with a genuinely TRANSPARENT background, arranged as exactly 4 columns x 2 rows of eight equally sized animation cells, each 384x512. NO panel lines, labels, checkerboard, shadows, or opaque background. Every frame is a standalone isolated flame cluster. Keep generous transparent gutters. Each frame has a common ground/bottom pivot at cell coordinate (192,440); every visible fire stays inside x=65..319 and y=72..442 in its cell. Small steady base, three irregular overlapping tongues of flame, occasional tiny detached ember. This is a compact equipment fire, NOT a bonfire with logs and NOT an explosion. Seen from the game's elevated camera with a slightly flattened elliptical base and upright screen-up flame height.

ART: match the reference's careful pixel construction: crisp hard-edged small pixel clusters and stepped contours; internal flame folds and small turbulent branching tongues, localized depth, no painted blur or smooth vector curves. Dark burnt copper and muted brick-red outer folds, burnt orange midtones, amber interior, very small warm ivory hottest cores. Luminous fire but NO neon, bloom, radial halo, lens flare, white floodlight, thick black outline, or glossy 3D product-render finish. Detailed enough to feel drawn for the reference room, clear when displayed around 70-100 screen pixels tall. Color limited and cohesive. No smoke in this sheet; smoke will be layered separately.

ANIMATION: eight consecutive frames read left-to-right across top row, then bottom row. A gentle 1-second looping fire, with tongues growing, curling sideways, separating and reforming; keep root position, scale, base width, brightness and flame mass consistent. The last frame should transition naturally back to the first. Actual shape changes, not eight duplicates or eight different kinds of fire. Final image contains only the eight flame-effect frames over alpha.
flame_alpha_retry: Edit this sprite sheet. Preserve all eight orange flame sprites and their exact pixels, shapes, colors, and positions. REMOVE the entire gray and white checkerboard and ALL gray/white backdrop pixels between and around the flames. Output a PNG with a REAL transparent alpha channel: empty areas must have alpha=0, not any representation of transparency. The checkerboard is unwanted image content, not an artistic part of the sheet. Do NOT redraw a checkerboard, white canvas, black canvas, colored background, floor, drop shadows or grid. Final result: eight flame sprites only, isolated over genuinely transparent alpha, same 1536x1024 canvas and 4x2 layout. Preserve flame ivory highlights as part of the foreground. No other changes.
smoke:
Create one production SMOKE animation sprite sheet for BrineSpace, an underwater industrial station game. Supplied reactor room image is a style reference ONLY: elevated south-facing cutaway game camera, carefully drawn pixel clusters, selective detail, subdued slate materials. DO NOT reproduce the room or machinery.

Exactly 1536x1024 PNG, exactly 4 columns x 2 rows, eight equal 384x512 animation cells. Each cell contains one isolated small rising smoke plume. SOURCE MATTE: perfectly flat solid vivid magenta #ff00ff everywhere outside the smoke. This magenta is a removable production background, NOT part of the smoke. No checkerboard, no grid lines, labels, text, shadows, floor or other objects.

Muted charcoal and warm slate smoke from a small electrical machinery fire: tapered thin bottom stem at cell (192,440), irregular layered curls rising screen-up, wider diffuse-looking but pixel-defined upper wisps. Keep within x=72..312 and y=60..444. Compact grey-brown smoke, mostly dark enough for restrained industrial game art but with mid-grey shaped folds readable against a dark room. Deliberate crisp small pixel clusters, stepped silhouettes, 8-12 closely related charcoal/slate/taupe shades, transparent-looking open gaps between wisps represented by the pure magenta matte. NO smooth airbrush, gaussian blur, fluffy cartoon cloud balls, thick outline, magical fog or neon. No flame or embers in this sheet.

Eight consecutive frames of a looping rising plume left-to-right then next row. Rolling curls travel upward, split into wisps, reform from the same fixed small root, with consistent mass, density and scale; last frame flows back to first. Preserve fixed bottom pivot and even gutters. Suitable for a reusable 70-100 pixel-high gameplay smoke effect layered separately over a fire.
embers:
Create one production EMBERS AND SPARKS animation sprite sheet for BrineSpace. Use the attached industrial room only as a reference for refined crisp pixel-art cluster size, muted copper/amber accent palette and elevated cutaway game viewpoint. Do not draw room, machinery, fixtures, backdrop objects or words.

Canvas exactly 1536x1024, eight equal cells in exactly 4 columns x 2 rows, each 384x512. Background is perfectly FLAT SOLID MAGENTA #ff00ff as a removable production matte. No checkerboard or texture in background, no framing or grid or labels.

Each cell contains a small airy spray of 10-15 tiny glowing cinders thrown upward from a fixed origin at local (192,440). Individual irregular pixel-chip silhouettes and a few very short trailing streaks. Restrained copper-orange and muted amber, occasional small warm ivory core, dark rust-red cooling fragments. Shaded intentional pixel clusters, only about 2-5 pixels per tiny ember at intended 96px gameplay height. NOT cartoon stars, not fireworks, not a fountain, no horizontal explosion rays, no flames, no smoke, no large chunks, no radial glow, bloom, or opaque dark halo. Air and open space dominate; embers occupy at most 3% of each cell. Keep all visible pixels within x=88..300 and y=68..448.

Eight consecutive animation frames: embers rise gently, drift outward asymmetrically and cool, fresh tiny cinders appear at the root as upper cinders fade; looping with similar coverage at first and last frame. Root, overall extent and scale consistent. Read left-to-right then second row. It must read as small mechanical-fire cinders in the supplied game's detailed understated art language, not a decorative magic sparkle effect.
